# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 11 (Bi-Vb Ss11)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Ss11
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 11
**Title (English, from literature):** Accusing nuns of acting from bias
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul5.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Adhikaraṇakupita* constitutes the eleventh *Saṅghādisesa* disciplinary training rule for nuns (*bhikkhunī*) in the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule concerns a nun who becomes resentful when a formal monastic legal issue (*adhikaraṇa*) is not settled according to her preference, and who persistently alleges that the community of nuns acted out of bias or partiality; upon formal admonition, failure to desist results in a Saṅghādisesa suspension. In modern English, it has been translated by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 Parallels exist in the Pali *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (Ss 11) and *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* (Ss 11), as well as in the Bhikṣuṇī Vinaya and Pātimokkha traditions preserved in Chinese for the Dharmaguptaka (Ss 17), Mahīśāsaka (Ss 16), Sarvāstivāda (Ss 15), Mūlasarvāstivāda (Ss 14), and Mahāsāṅghika (Ss 15) schools. It also survives in the Tibetan translation of the Mūlasarvāstivāda *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (Ss 14) and in Sanskrit in the Mahāsāṅghika-Lokottaravāda *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* (Ss 15).
